version.changelog:
v5.11.3 – Security Declaration Alignment

This release fixes security-scan findings caused by inconsistent runtime declarations in v5.11.2.

What changed

• Updated runtime declarations to match actual workflow behavior:
• requires_binaries: true
• requires_credentials: true
• requires_network: true
• Clarified package behavior:
• The package itself remains documentation-only (no install-time executable payload).
• Agent workflows may execute shell/network actions at runtime when invoked by the user.
• Added explicit runtime transparency:
• Required/optional runtime binaries
• Optional credentials/environment expectations (e.g. GH_TOKEN, Claude auth, MCP configuration)
• Refined security semantics to distinguish:
• install-time safety
• runtime agent capabilities

Why this release

v5.11.2 could create a misleading security impression by claiming no network/credentials/code-execution requirements while documenting workflows that use shell, GitHub, Playwright, and web tools.
v5.11.3 resolves that mismatch for clearer trust and more accurate scanner interpretation.

Compatibility

• No breaking workflow changes
• Backward-compatible behavior
• Metadata/security declaration update only

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cc-godmode
Version: 5.11.3

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its extensive use of high-risk capabilities, including broad `Bash` execution, file system modification (`Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `mkdir`), and network access (`WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `GitHub MCP`, `Playwright MCP`). While these capabilities are explicitly declared in `SKILL.md` and `clawdis.yaml` and are plausibly necessary for an 'autonomous multi-agent development workflow,' they inherently present a significant attack surface. The `SKILL.md` and other documentation files also serve as a prompt injection surface for the AI agent, even though the current instructions do not contain explicit malicious commands. The transparency about runtime requirements and the explicit instruction 'NEVER git push without permission' mitigate against a 'malicious' classification, but the inherent power granted to the agent warrants a 'suspicious' label.

llm.summary: This docs-only orchestration skill is transparent, but it gives agents broad runtime authority over code, screenshots, and GitHub operations without enough scoping or confirmation guidance.

dimensions.detail: Network, local binaries, Playwright, GitHub MCP/gh, and credentials are disclosed as runtime expectations. These are proportionate for full development automation, but users should avoid running it against production accounts or sensitive pages without controls.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package appears documentation-only, with no executable scripts or install-time code in the inspected artifact. Manual installation commands copy the skill into an OpenClaw or Clawdbot skills directory.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill emphasizes autonomous workflow execution and mandatory agent steps. It includes a clear permission rule for git push, but does not similarly gate GitHub issue, PR merge, release, or branch-deletion commands, and screenshot capture is mandatory without sensitivity/redaction guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor, service, hook, or automatic persistence was found. The skill writes reports under project folders and may use optional memory MCP for research findings; this is disclosed but should be scoped by the user.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: multi-agent development orchestration. The documented runtime capabilities are broad and include file edits, Bash, web access, Playwright, GitHub operations, credentials, and optional memory, which fit the purpose but create high-impact authority.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to coordinate substantial development work. Use least-privilege GitHub tokens, require human confirmation before PR merges/releases/issue closures, run Playwright only against test or sanitized accounts, review screenshots before sharing or committing them, and pin or locally install MCP packages rather than using unpinned npx/global installs.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: Mandatory screenshots are expected for the tester role, but the artifact does not warn about PII/secrets or define redaction and retention for .playwright-mcp artifacts.
[SQP-2] expected: GitHub commands are expected for the github-manager role, but ready-to-run create, close, merge, release, and branch-deletion commands lack explicit confirmation gates beyond the separate git push rule.
[SQP-2] expected: The optional rm CLAUDE.md migration step is purpose-aligned and user-run, but it is a destructive deletion command with only limited warning to keep project-specific instructions.
[AS3] expected: The cited grep reads this skill's own installed SKILL.md to check its version; this is not evidence of peer-skill snooping.
[RP1] expected: The unpinned npx/playwright-mcp troubleshooting commands are not automatically executed by the skill, but they create a real supply-chain risk if users follow them.
[T08] expected: The static scan's unpinned third-party MCP package concern is supported by the troubleshooting guide; it is a caution about mutable npm package execution, not evidence of bundled malicious code.
